content: These infrastructural breakdowns resulted in billions of rands in lost revenue, fundamentally forcing mining companies to reassess their operational and procurement strategies [33] . To mitigate the ongoing impacts of supply chain bottlenecks, mining fleet operators are increasingly directing their procurement efforts toward investments in advanced, highly resilient equipment that can withstand infrastructural unpredictability [33] . The broader challenges facing supply chains have been further corroborated at industry events such as the Transport Evolution Africa Expo, which, alongside recaps of the Mining Indaba, underscores the paramount importance of strategic and adaptive procurement in South Africa’s mining sector [32][35] . Concurrently, legislative developments have introduced new imperatives into the procurement processes of mining fleets. The implementation of the Climate Change Act 22 of 2024, which officially came into effect in 2025, has become a primary driver for the adoption of comprehensive decarbonization measures across the industry [34] . This regulatory shift is pushing mining companies to rigorously integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) criteria into their procurement decisions to ensure compliance with increasingly strict emissions standards . Recent industry gatherings, such as the Mining Fleet Southern Africa 2026 event, have similarly reflected this transition; while specific historical procurement transactions were not the primary focus, the overarching emphasis on future planning and sustainability strongly suggests that modern procurement strategies are centered on adapting to these new market and regulatory landscapes rather than adhering to traditional, legacy practices [35] . While procurement strategies are evolving rapidly in response to macro-environmental pressures, identifying the specific service needs of mining operators presents a more nuanced challenge due to the fragmented nature of available market data as of July 2026. The intersection of these evolving procurement methods and opaque service needs directly informs the factors influencing provider selection and collaboration within the South African mining sector. Furthermore, the integration of ESG criteria into procurement frameworks means that provider selection is increasingly contingent upon the ability to supply and service environmentally sustainable fleet options.
